# Bio

![](images/Basham_headshot.jpg){fig-align="center" width="284"}

Dr. C Andrew Basham, B.A., M.Sc., Ph.D.

My goal as an epidemiologist is to advance causal inference in the
epidemiological research to enable individuals and communities to
contribute to the design and interpretation of statistical analyses
describing their lived experiences and influencing the policies,
programs, and practices that impact their lives.

The skills and knowledge I bring to teaching are built on research
integrity: relevance, rigour, reviewability, and reproducibility.

I am an epidemiologist specializing in causal inference based on
observational data analyses. I have extensive data science experience
using SAS and R to manage and analyze large relational healthcare
databases in collaborative coding environments to produce decision-grade
evidence. I educate trainees in epidemiology and biostatistics -
grounded in the principles of open science - through practical research
experience.

My research interests include critical illness survivorship,
pharmacoepidemiology (drug safety and effectiveness), pharmacoequity,
drug utilization, public health program performance measurement,
infectious disease modelling, violence epidemiology, race and ethnicity
data, and missing data generating mechanisms, their structures,
patterns, associations, and implications for research, policy, and
practice.

Sincerely,

**C. Andrew Basham, PhD**
